\label{lemma-spell-out-degree-zero-cycle}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be proper over $k$. Let $\alpha = \sum n_i[Z_i]$
be in $Z_0(X)$. Then
$$
\deg(\alpha) = \sum n_i\deg(Z_i)
$$
where $\deg(Z_i)$ is the degree of $Z_i \to \Spec(k)$, i.e.,
$\deg(Z_i) = \dim_k \Gamma(Z_i, \mathcal{O}_{Z_i})$.
statement:
A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $T$ and a zero-cycle $\gamma=\sum n_i[x_i]$, define $\deg(\gamma)=\sum n_i[\kappa(x_i):k]$. For a locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of constant rank $r$ on a proper scheme of dimension at most one, set $\deg(\mathcal E)=\chi(T,\mathcal E)-r\chi(T,\mathcal O_T)$, where $\chi(T,\mathcal F)=\sum_j(-1)^j\dim_kH^j(T,\mathcal F)$.

\label{lemma-degree-vector-bundle}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ of dimension $\leq 1$.
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of constant
rank. Then
$$
\deg(\mathcal{E}) = \deg(c_1(\mathcal{E}) \cap [X]_1)
$$
where the left hand side is defined in
Varieties, Definition \ref{varieties-definition-degree-invertible-sheaf}.
statement:
A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a nonzero meromorphic section $u$ of an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$, $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ is the Weil divisor with local coefficients given by the order of the representing meromorphic function in a trivialization at each codimension-one integral closed subscheme. Its Chow class is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. A global section $u$ has scheme-theoretic zero locus $Z(u)$. The operation $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ is defined by restriction to each integral component $W$ and proper pushforward to $T$, and descends to Chow groups.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a proper $k$-scheme $T$ and a zero-cycle $\gamma=\sum n_i[x_i]$, define $\deg(\gamma)=\sum n_i[\kappa(x_i):k]$. For a locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of constant rank $r$ on a proper scheme of dimension at most one, set $\deg(\mathcal E)=\chi(T,\mathcal E)-r\chi(T,\mathcal O_T)$, where $\chi(T,\mathcal F)=\sum_j(-1)^j\dim_kH^j(T,\mathcal F)$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ of dimension $\leq 1$.
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of constant
rank. Then
$$
\deg(\mathcal{E}) = \deg(c_1(\mathcal{E}) \cap [X]_1)
$$
where $\deg(\mathcal E)=\chi(X,\mathcal E)-\operatorname{rank}(\mathcal E)\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$.

\label{lemma-degrees-and-numerical-intersections}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$.
Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme of dimension $d$.
Let $\mathcal{L}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{L}_d$ be invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Then
$$
(\mathcal{L}_1 \cdots \mathcal{L}_d \cdot Z) =
\deg(
c_1(\mathcal{L}_1) \cap \ldots \cap c_1(\mathcal{L}_d) \cap [Z]_d)
$$
where the left hand side is defined in
Varieties, Definition \ref{varieties-definition-intersection-number}.
In particular,
$$
\deg_\mathcal{L}(Z) = \deg(c_1(\mathcal{L})^d \cap [Z]_d)
$$
if $\mathcal{L}$ is an ample invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.

For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. For a proper $k$-scheme $T$ and a zero-cycle $\gamma=\sum n_i[x_i]$, define $\deg(\gamma)=\sum n_i[\kappa(x_i):k]$. For a locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of constant rank $r$ on a proper scheme of dimension at most one, set $\deg(\mathcal E)=\chi(T,\mathcal E)-r\chi(T,\mathcal O_T)$, where $\chi(T,\mathcal F)=\sum_j(-1)^j\dim_kH^j(T,\mathcal F)$.

For a proper $d$-dimensional $k$-scheme $Z$ and invertible $\mathcal L_1,\ldots,\mathcal L_d$, the numerical intersection $(\mathcal L_1\cdots\mathcal L_d\cdot Z)$ is the coefficient of $n_1\cdots n_d$ in the degree-$d$ polynomial $\chi(Z,\mathcal L_1^{\otimes n_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal L_d^{\otimes n_d})$. For an ample $\mathcal L$, $\deg_{\mathcal L}(Z)$ is $d!$ times the leading coefficient of $\chi(Z,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$.
